lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 148, which makes CI's verify job faster while still running every test before the merge.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one forty-eight, which makes C I's verify job faster while still running every test before the merge.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The verify job now picks its tests, posts fewer shots, uploads them in one commit, and runs four tests at a time.
First, a new step picks the tests: the smoke test and the PR's own tests, or all of them.
The tests then run four at a time instead of two, and the run records how many it ran.
Only the smoke test, the PR's own tests and failed tests get numbered shots. The rest get a result only.
All the shots go to the shots branch in a single commit, instead of one commit per file.
The verify comment says whether the run was partial or ran all tests, and lists the other passing tests on one line.
While a run is partial, the summary shows an hourglass instead of ready for review, and the digest reports the scope.
Before the merge, the agent pushes a commit marked Verify: full, which runs every test again.
A full run took about 25 minutes, and most runs are early pushes like review fixes. Those now get short.
Nothing is dropped, only moved: the merge still needs a run of every test on the final commit.
Every test runs on a push to main, on a Verify: full commit, or when the PR changes the verify scripts or the workflow.
The run script now takes the list of tests to run, and writes down the scope and which tests are the PR's own.
The shots of the other passing tests aren't posted, but they stay in the run's downloadable artifact.
The upload script makes every file, then one tree and one commit, and redoes the commit if another run moved the branch.
A partial run's comment also says how to run every test.
The verify status now carries a full flag, which the summary and the digest agent read.
The merge rule now needs verify to have run all tests on the head commit.
An early push to a feature PR runs the smoke test and its own tests.
A Verify: full commit, a change to the CI files, or a push to main runs all of them.
A Verify trailer with an unknown value gives a warning and a partial run.
Before, each file was its own commit, and two runs committing at once caused most of the old failures.
Now each run makes one commit, and remakes it on the new tip when the branch moved, up to eight times.
A file that can't be uploaded is removed from the branch, so no stale shot stays behind, and the job fails.
When a file is lost, shots.sh writes down why, and the error the job reports quotes that reason.
The PR changes four CI scripts, the summary script, the workflow, two skill files, the digest agent and CLAUDE.md.
To undo it, revert the merge commit. To force a full run on one PR, push a Verify: full commit.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The building session used stand-ins for GitHub and Thunar. Then this PR's CI ran the real suite and upload twice.
The timings to beat come from the issue: tests took about 12 minutes, and the upload about 9 and a half.
The new upload keeps the old script's retry rules and link format.
Against a fake GitHub, the upload made one commit, redid it when the branch moved, and handled a missing file.
On a fake run, only three shots were numbered, and the comment said the run was partial.
Running three named tests ran just those, after fixing a bug where the list was ignored.
In this PR's two full CI runs, all 32 tests passed at four at a time, and the shots went up in one commit.
The tests step took 370 and 369 seconds, against 733 on main at two at a time.
lines.say: The tests step took three hundred seventy and three sixty-nine seconds, against seven thirty-three on main at two at a time.

lines.caption: Each test kept its time within five seconds, except test 14 once, which took 14 seconds longer.
lines.say: Each test kept its time within five seconds, except test fourteen once, which took fourteen seconds longer.

lines.caption: The upload step fell from about 9.5 minutes to 8 or 9 seconds, and the whole verify job to about 400 seconds.
lines.say: The upload step fell from about nine and a half minutes to eight or nine seconds, and the whole verify job to about four hundred seconds.

lines.caption: The build job's time varied with apt and its cache, not with this PR.
A local review before the first push found 7 issues: six were fixed and one was kept. Then CI reviewed every push.
lines.say: A local review before the first push found seven issues: six were fixed and one was kept. Then C I reviewed every push.

lines.caption: The fixes covered how results were counted, some wording, and removing a failed upload's old copy.
CI's review found 49 issues over ten rounds. None was medium or high after the first half, and every medium was fixed.
lines.say: C I's review found forty-nine issues over ten rounds. None was medium or high after the first half, and every medium was fixed.

lines.caption: The owner accepted the risk of flaky runs at four at a time, after both measured runs passed with steady test times.
The owner also accepted six low findings about error wording, after nine rounds kept finding new ones.
Eleven unconfirmed low findings from later reviews count as accepted under the repo's rules.
Late in the review, the upload's error handling was reworked so each failure reports one error with its reason.
A partial run, a full run and a failing test can only be seen on a later PR, since this one always runs everything.
The hourglass summary first shows on the first feature PR after the merge.
The PR, its two CI runs and the main run they were compared with are all linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No issue depends on this one, so what follows is the rest of its test plan.
This PR's own CI runs are done: all 32 tests passed twice, in about half the old time.
Then a trial PR checks a partial run, a full run, and a test that fails on purpose.
From then on, every PR ends with a Verify: full push before the merge.
Four at a time held up, so it stays at four, and the upload took one commit and a few seconds.
The trial PR adds a trivial test, then pushes Verify: full, then breaks another test to see its shots posted.
After that, early pushes stay short, and the last push before each merge runs every test.
In short: quick runs while a PR is being fixed, and one full run before it merges.
